requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation maps to code reachable from the `{impl}` items, and each has a test carrying a `{test}` reference.

**Initial set.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]` first collects the subject, the cited requirements, the reference-owning outline nodes and the anchors. It then calls `definition_inputs` with those mandatory inputs and `Some(&subject.text)`. That calls `crate::terms::dependencies`, which has two steps:
- `direct_references` gathers terms from the subject text and from each contributed input. For Requirements and Markdown inputs it scans declaration bodies. For Rust it scans only comments. For a Definition input it takes the named definition itself.
- `close_dependencies` expands those terms to a fixed point. Its `visited` and `required` sets give "without duplicates" and "nontermination on cycles". It also returns the transitive definitions.

`definition_inputs` turns each result into an `InputSelector::Definition` input via `source_input`, which resolves the full declaration text. `prepare` appends only dependencies not already in the set. The mandatory set is supplied in the first request, because `converse` in `src/authoring/mod.rs` starts `pending` from `sources.mandatory_inputs()`.

**Additional reads.**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[read]` calls `additional_definitions`, which runs `definition_inputs` over the delivered input. It filters out inputs already delivered or already recorded, so there are no duplicates. It returns the definitions with the read result.
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[ResultPages]/fn[deliver]` uses `additional_definitions` and `definitions_each` for paged line-range reads.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` pushes the delivered inputs, including the definitions, onto `pending`. It records them with `sources.record_inputs(&pending)` only after the next response arrives. A submission is accepted only after that step, so the definitions are supplied and recorded before acceptance.

**Tests.**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` builds terms `unit` and `value` that reference each other, so they form a cycle. It asserts exactly 2 definition inputs.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms]` shows a term referenced from a contributed source becomes a mandatory input.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission]` asserts these points:
  - the transitive set is `terms.unit` and `terms.value`, once each;
  - each definition's text begins with `:::{definition}` followed by `:phrase:`;
  - the definitions appear in the second request, before the submission;
  - they appear in the recorded evidence.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` and `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` cover definitions delivered with item reads, line-range reads and pages.

I found no unspecified behavior in the `{impl}` code that the requirement doesn't cover.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
